title: Open cloze: the outage
instructions: Escribí UNA palabra gramatical en cada hueco.
text: Last night our website [1] down for almost two hours. I was having dinner when my phone rang. My colleague Ana [2] been working on the problem for an hour, but she had not found the cause [3]. By the time I got to the office, she [4] already fixed it. It was a bug [5] had been introduced in the last update.

items.e: Estado en el pasado: the website WAS down.
had + been + -ing: duración antes de otro evento pasado.
En negativo, 'yet' va al final: had not found the cause yet.
'By the time I got there' → ya lo había arreglado: had + participio.
Cosa (a bug) + sujeto de 'had been introduced' → that / which.

Lugar → where.

got used to it (pronombre objeto).

title: Multiple choice cloze: the power cut
instructions: Elegí la opción correcta para cada hueco.
text: While Marta [1] on a new feature, the office lost power. She [2] not saved her work, so she lost two hours of code. Her boss, [3] was very kind, told her not to worry. Marta [4] to save her work only once a day, but now she saves it every ten minutes. It was a lesson [5] she never forgot.

items.e: While + acción en progreso interrumpida.
had not saved: anterior a lost.
Entre comas (non-defining) → who; that no.
Hábito pasado: used to save.
Cosa → which / that.

title: Multiple choice cloze: Diego's first months
instructions: Elegí la opción correcta para cada hueco.
text: When Diego joined the team, he [1] never worked with microservices, so he was not [2] the tools at first. He [3] used to them after a few months, and now he is the person [4] everyone asks for help. The application [5] he built last year is now in production.

items.e: had never worked: anterior a 'joined'.
was not used TO + sustantivo.
'after a few months' → proceso completado → got used to.
Persona → who.
Cosa; the application (which) he built: objeto, podría omitirse.

title: Gapped text: the migration
instructions: Cinco oraciones fueron eliminadas del texto. Elegí de la lista (A-H) la que encaja en cada hueco. Hay TRES oraciones que sobran.
text: Last spring, Julia's team decided to move their application to a new cloud provider. [1] They had been using the old system for six years, and everyone was used to it. On the first day of the migration, Julia was checking the logs when the database suddenly stopped responding. [2] She called her colleague Pablo, who was working from home at that time. [3] By the time he connected, she had already restarted two services, but nothing had changed. Pablo, whose experience with databases was much greater, found the problem in ten minutes. [4] Someone had deleted an important configuration file the day before. After that, they created a backup system. [5] Julia says she would never make the same mistake again.
bank: It was not an easy decision.
For a moment, she did not know what to do.
It was late, and he had been sleeping for an hour.
The cause was simple but serious.
The system has worked perfectly ever since.
Julia used to work for a company that sold books.
They are moving to a new office next month.
Pablo has never liked working from home.

a: It was not an easy decision.
items.e: 'It' = la decisión; luego 'They had been using the old system...' explica por qué.

a: For a moment, she did not know what to do.
items.e: Reacción a que la base de datos dejó de responder; sigue 'She called...'.

a: It was late, and he had been sleeping for an hour.
items.e: Explica por qué tardó en conectarse ('By the time he connected').

a: The cause was simple but serious.

title: Sara's first job
instructions: Leé el texto y elegí la respuesta correcta para cada pregunta.
text:
When Sara started her first job as a developer, she was very nervous. She had studied programming for two years, but she had never worked in a real team before. In her first week, her manager, who was a very patient person, gave her a small task: to fix a bug in the login page.
Sara used to think that professional developers never made mistakes, but that day she discovered the opposite. While she was testing her solution, the whole website went down. She had deleted a line of code that other parts of the application needed. Everyone in the office looked at her, and she wanted to disappear.
Her manager, however, laughed and said, "We have all done that. Do you know how long I had been working here when I broke the server for the first time? Three days!" Together they repaired the site in twenty minutes.
Sara remembers that moment as the day she stopped being afraid. Now, two years later, she is used to working under pressure, and she helps the new members of the team, who are as nervous as she was.

items.q: What did Sara have before she started the job?
o: Two years of study but no experience in a team
items.a: Two years of study but no experience in a team
items.e: 'She had studied programming for two years, but ... had never worked in a real team'.

items.q: What did Sara think about professional developers?
items.e: 'used to think that professional developers never made mistakes'.

items.q: What happened while she was testing her solution?
items.e: 'the whole website went down'.

items.q: What did the manager say about mistakes?
o: He also made a big one early in his career
items.a: He also made a big one early in his career
items.e: 'We have all done that ... I broke the server ... Three days!'.

items.q: How does Sara feel about working under pressure now?
items.e: 'she is used to working under pressure' (be used to = estar acostumbrada).

title: Legacy code
instructions: Leé el texto y elegí la respuesta correcta.
text: Many developers dislike working with legacy code, which is software that was written years ago and is still used today. Often, the people who created it have left the company, and the documentation, if it exists, is out of date. Junior developers who are not used to reading other people's code find this especially frustrating. However, experienced programmers know that legacy systems have an important advantage: they have been tested by real users for years, so the bugs that would have appeared in a new product were fixed long ago. Before rewriting a system from scratch, teams should ask themselves whether the risk is worth it. Many companies that decided to start again lost months of work, and some of them never managed to reproduce the reliability of the original.

items.q: Why do junior developers often find legacy code frustrating?
o: They are not accustomed to reading code written by others
items.a: They are not accustomed to reading code written by others
items.e: 'not used to reading other people's code'.

items.q: What advantage of legacy systems does the writer mention?
o: Users have already helped find and fix many of their bugs
Their authors still work at the company
items.a: Users have already helped find and fix many of their bugs
items.e: 'tested by real users for years ... bugs were fixed long ago'.
